easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Doth not wisdom cry? and understanding put forth her voice?”
easy.q: Who cries aloud in these verses?

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of man.”
She stands in high places, by the way, and at the city gates and doors.
easy.q: Where does Wisdom stand and cry?

answers: So she can address many people
So she can hide from the public
medium.explanation: These public locations allow Wisdom to call openly to the sons of man.
medium.q: Why does Wisdom call from roads, gates, and doors?

medium.explanation: Wisdom cries, and understanding puts forth her voice.
medium.q: What relationship between wisdom and understanding appears in verse 1?

answers: She first calls kings, then men
She first hides, then keeps silent
She cries, then calls to the sons of man
medium.explanation: The passage first describes her voice and then her direct call to people.
medium.q: Which order correctly describes Wisdom’s actions?

answers: Her message is intended for a wide audience
She is intended only for palace residents
She does not want anyone to listen
challenge.explanation: Her public locations and universal address show that her message is broadly available.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Wisdom calling in open places?

challenge.explanation: She calls aloud from visible and central places.
challenge.q: Which feature of Wisdom’s call is emphasized?

answers: Wisdom belongs to one house only
Wisdom seeks people where they pass and gather
challenge.explanation: The locations emphasize Wisdom’s desire to reach people in public spaces.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of places such as the way, gates, and doors suggest?

paragraphs.title: Truth, Integrity, and the Value of Wisdom

easy.explanation: Verse 5 addresses the simple and fools, calling them to gain understanding.
easy.q: Whom does Wisdom call to understand?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “For my mouth shall speak truth.”
Verse 11 says wisdom is better than rubies, and all desirable things cannot compare with it.

medium.explanation: She calls the simple to understand wisdom and fools to have an understanding heart.
medium.q: What does Wisdom ask the simple and fools to gain?

answers: Her words are upright and right
Her words are only for judges
medium.explanation: The surrounding verses say that her words contain nothing froward or perverse.
medium.q: What does “all the words of my mouth are in righteousness” mean?

answers: Because it is kept in a palace
Because its words are true and upright
medium.explanation: The passage praises Wisdom’s truth and righteousness above silver, gold, and precious stones.
medium.q: Why is Wisdom more valuable than treasures?

answers: Truth and righteousness versus wickedness and perversity
challenge.explanation: Wisdom speaks truth and righteousness, while wickedness and perversity are rejected.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in this passage?

answers: Wisdom is offered to those lacking experience and understanding
Wisdom is only for the wealthy
challenge.explanation: Her invitation includes people who need instruction and understanding.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Wisdom addressing both the simple and fools?

answers: Wisdom is worth only a little money
Wisdom is superior to material riches
challenge.explanation: The passage declares that wisdom is better than rubies and choice gold.
challenge.q: What view of material wealth is expressed by the comparison with gold and rubies?

paragraphs.title: Wisdom’s Qualities and Influence on Leadership

answers: Evil, pride, and a froward mouth
easy.explanation: Verses 13–14 identify evil, pride, arrogancy, the evil way, and the froward mouth as things Wisdom hates.

answers: Counsel, sound wisdom, understanding, and strength
easy.explanation: Verse 14 says, “Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom: I am understanding; I have strength.”
Verses 15–16 mention kings, princes, nobles, and judges.
easy.q: Who is influenced by Wisdom in leadership?

medium.explanation: By Wisdom, kings reign and princes decree justice.

answers: Riches, honor, lasting riches, and righteousness
medium.explanation: Verses 17–18 connect loving and seeking Wisdom with finding her, riches, honor, and righteousness.
medium.q: What does Wisdom promise those who love and seek her?

answers: The fear of the LORD is joined with hatred of evil
medium.explanation: Verse 13 directly says, “The fear of the LORD is to hate evil.”
medium.q: What connection is made between the fear of the LORD and hating evil?

answers: Wisdom is only for family life
challenge.explanation: Rulers and judges need Wisdom to govern and decree justice.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Wisdom being needed by kings and judges?

answers: She hates pride and evil and therefore guides people toward justice
She loves evil and therefore brings poverty
She hates counsel and prevents leadership
challenge.explanation: Her hatred of evil and pride is connected with righteous rule and judgment.
challenge.q: What relationship does the passage create between Wisdom’s qualities and her results?

challenge.explanation: The expression describes people who diligently seek Wisdom and therefore find her.
challenge.q: What does “those that seek me early” mean in context?

answers: In the beginning of His way
easy.explanation: Verse 22 says, “The LORD possessed me in the beginning of his way.”
easy.q: When was Wisdom possessed by the LORD?

easy.explanation: Wisdom is described as present before the depths, fountains, mountains, hills, earth, and dust.
easy.q: What existed before the things described in these verses?

easy.explanation: These natural features are listed as existing after Wisdom was already present.
easy.q: Which created things are mentioned as coming after Wisdom?

answers: The beginning associated with the LORD’s work
A physical road in a city
medium.explanation: Wisdom is presented as present at the beginning of the LORD’s works.
medium.q: What does “the beginning of his way” mean here?

answers: Wisdom, then depths and mountains, then earth
medium.explanation: Wisdom precedes the depths, mountains, hills, and earth.

answers: Wisdom existed before the things that had not yet been made
medium.explanation: The wording repeatedly places Wisdom before the natural world was formed.
medium.q: What is emphasized by “before” and “or ever”?

answers: Wisdom is merely a human skill
challenge.explanation: Wisdom is associated with the LORD’s beginning and precedes the creation described.
challenge.q: What view of Wisdom emerges from this passage?

answers: Wisdom is connected with an order preceding creation
challenge.explanation: The passage places Wisdom before the depths, mountains, earth, and dust.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Wisdom preceding the natural world?

answers: Wisdom preceded even the highest part of the dust of the world
Wisdom appears only after the earth
Wisdom has no connection with creation
challenge.explanation: Verse 26 says Wisdom was present before the highest part of the dust of the world.
challenge.q: Which easily overlooked detail is important?

paragraphs.title: Wisdom in the Ordering of the World

easy.explanation: Verse 27 says, “When he prepared the heavens, I was there.”
easy.q: With whom was Wisdom when the heavens were prepared?

easy.explanation: The LORD gave the sea His decree so that the waters should not pass His commandment.
easy.q: What was established concerning the sea?

easy.explanation: Verse 31 says, “my delights were with the sons of men.”

answers: Preparing the heavens, limiting the waters, and appointing the earth’s foundations
medium.explanation: The passage describes the heavens, deep, sea, clouds, fountains, and foundations of the earth.

answers: She is present in the description of the sea being given limits
medium.explanation: The passage describes the sea receiving a decree so its waters would not pass the commandment.
medium.q: What is Wisdom’s relationship to the sea’s boundaries?

answers: Rejoicing before the LORD and delighting in the inhabited earth and people
medium.explanation: Wisdom rejoices before the LORD and has delights with the sons of men.
medium.q: How is Wisdom described at the end of the passage?

answers: Wisdom is connected with order and organization
Wisdom is connected only with wealth
challenge.explanation: She is present as the heavens, waters, and foundations of the earth are ordered.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Wisdom’s connection with the laws of nature?

answers: From the ordering of creation to delight in humanity
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the heavens and sea to Wisdom’s rejoicing in the inhabited earth and people.
challenge.q: What conceptual movement occurs in these verses?

answers: An ongoing relationship of joy and delight
challenge.explanation: The word “daily” presents continuing delight and rejoicing before the LORD.
challenge.q: What does “I was daily his delight” suggest?

paragraphs.title: An Invitation to Listen and Find Life

easy.explanation: Verse 32 begins, “Now therefore hearken unto me, O ye children.”
easy.q: To whom does Wisdom speak at the beginning of this passage?

answers: Hear instruction and keep her ways
easy.explanation: The passage calls them to hear instruction, be wise, and keep Wisdom’s ways.
easy.q: What does Wisdom ask her hearers to do?

answers: Life and favour from the LORD
easy.explanation: Verse 35 says, “Whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of the LORD.”
easy.q: What does the person who finds Wisdom find?

medium.explanation: “Daily” and “waiting” portray continued attention to Wisdom.
medium.q: What does “watching daily at my gates” suggest?

answers: Keeping her ways is presented as a path to blessing
Keeping her ways leads to wickedness
medium.explanation: Verse 32 says, “blessed are they that keep my ways.”
medium.q: What connection is made between keeping Wisdom’s ways and blessedness?

medium.explanation: Verse 36 says, “he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul.”
medium.q: What happens to the person who sins against Wisdom?

answers: Finding Wisdom brings life, while hating Wisdom brings death
Hearing Wisdom brings wealth only, while rejecting her brings honor
Wisdom brings life and death equally
challenge.explanation: The final verses contrast finding Wisdom and receiving life with hating her and loving death.
challenge.q: What contrast summarizes the end of the chapter?

answers: Wisdom requires listening and accepting correction
challenge.explanation: The command joins attentive hearing with becoming wise and not rejecting instruction.
challenge.q: What does “Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not” imply?

answers: Daily waiting at Wisdom’s gates leads to finding her and life
Perseverance prevents a person from finding Wisdom
challenge.explanation: The passage commends daily waiting and then promises life to whoever finds Wisdom.
challenge.q: How is perseverance connected with finding life?
